questions.q: What's the core difference between Import and DirectQuery?
options: Import copies data into the Power BI file; DirectQuery leaves it in the source and queries it live
Import only works with Excel; DirectQuery only works with SQL
DirectQuery is always faster than Import
They are two names for the exact same behavior
questions.explain: Import brings a snapshot of the data into your file for fast, offline access. DirectQuery queries the source directly every time a visual loads, trading speed for always-current data.

questions.q: Why has this course used Import by default in every lesson so far?
options: It offers full feature support, fast visuals, and no dependency on a live connection while learning
DirectQuery isn't available in Power BI Desktop
Import is required for every data source
Import is the only mode that supports Excel files
questions.explain: Import gives full DAX support and fast, offline-capable visuals — the right default for learning and for most real reports, unless a specific reason (huge data, true real-time need, or a data-residency policy) calls for DirectQuery.

questions.q: Can you convert a table from Import mode to DirectQuery mode?
options: No — you can convert DirectQuery to Import, but never the reverse
Yes, freely, at any time
Only if the table has fewer than 1 million rows
Only for SQL Server sources
questions.explain: The conversion only goes one direction: DirectQuery to Import (or Dual). Once a table is set to Import, going back to DirectQuery requires reconnecting from scratch.

questions.q: In Table (Data) view, what happens when you select a DirectQuery table?
options: No data displays — a message explains DirectQuery data can't be shown this way
It shows the same cached data as an Import table
Power BI automatically converts it to Import to show the data
It shows only the column names, no rows
questions.explain: Table view displays cached data, which DirectQuery tables don't have stored locally — so Power BI shows a message instead of a data grid.

questions.q: What problem does Dual storage mode solve?
options: It lets small dimension tables behave as Import (fast) or DirectQuery (consistent) depending on what a query needs, when mixed with a large DirectQuery fact table
It doubles the row limit for DirectQuery sources
It allows two people to edit the same report simultaneously
It automatically encrypts DirectQuery connections
questions.explain: Dual tables act as Import when that's faster, or as DirectQuery when needed for consistency with a still-live fact table — a practical middle ground for mixed-mode models.
